references.title: Oscillations, waves, fluids, and thermodynamics
references.body:
## Oscillations

| | |
|---|---|
| SHM | $x = A\cos(\omega t + \phi)$; $a = -\omega^2x$ |
| Spring | $\omega = \sqrt{k/m}$, $T = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$ |
| Simple pendulum | $T = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$ |
| Physical pendulum | $T = 2\pi\sqrt{I/(mgd)}$ |
| Maxima | $v_{\max} = A\omega$, $a_{\max} = A\omega^2$; $E = \tfrac12kA^2$ |

## Waves and sound

| | |
|---|---|
| Wave speed | $v = f\lambda$; string: $v = \sqrt{F_T/\mu}$ |
| Traveling wave | $y = A\sin(kx - \omega t)$, $k = 2\pi/\lambda$, $\omega = 2\pi f$ |
| String fixed at both ends; open pipe | $f_n = \dfrac{nv}{2L}$, $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$ |
| Pipe closed at one end | $f_n = \dfrac{nv}{4L}$, $n = 1, 3, 5, \ldots$ |
| Intensity | $I = \dfrac{P}{4\pi r^2}$; $\beta = 10\log_{10}\dfrac{I}{I_0}$, $I_0 = 10^{-12}$ W/m² |
| Beats | $f_{\text{beat}} = \lvert f_1 - f_2\rvert$ |
| Doppler | $f' = f\dfrac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s}$ (upper signs: approaching) |

## Fluids

| | |
|---|---|
| Density, pressure | $\rho = m/V$, $P = F/A$ |
| Depth | $P = P_0 + \rho gh$ |
| Pascal | $F_1/A_1 = F_2/A_2$ |
| Buoyancy | $F_B = \rho_{\text{fluid}}V_{\text{disp}}g$ |
| Continuity | $A_1v_1 = A_2v_2$ |
| Bernoulli | $P + \tfrac12\rho v^2 + \rho gy$ = const |
| Torricelli | $v = \sqrt{2gh}$ |

## Heat and gases

| | |
|---|---|
| Expansion | $\Delta L = \alpha L\Delta T$ |
| Heat | $Q = mc\Delta T$; phase change $Q = mL$ |
| Conduction, radiation | $Q/t = kA\Delta T/L$; $P = e\sigma AT^4$ |
| Ideal gas | $PV = nRT = Nk_BT$ |
| Kinetic theory | $\tfrac12m\overline{v^2} = \tfrac32k_BT$; $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{3RT/M}$ |
| Monatomic gas | $E_{\text{int}} = \tfrac32nRT$; $C_V = \tfrac32R$, $C_P = \tfrac52R$, $\gamma = \tfrac53$ |

## Thermodynamics

| | |
|---|---|
| First law | $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = Q - W$ ($W$ by the gas); AP Physics 2 form: $\Delta U = Q + W$ with $W = -P\Delta V$ done *on* the gas |
| Work by gas | area under the $PV$ curve; isobaric $P\Delta V$; isothermal $nRT\ln(V_f/V_i)$ |
| Adiabatic | $PV^\gamma$ = const, $TV^{\gamma - 1}$ = const |
| Engine | $e = \dfrac{W}{Q_H} = 1 - \dfrac{Q_C}{Q_H}$; Carnot $e = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H}$ |
| Refrigerator | $K = Q_C/W$; Carnot $\dfrac{T_C}{T_H - T_C}$ |
| Entropy | $\Delta S = Q/T$ for heat $Q$ transferred at constant $T$ (e.g. melting, boiling, a large reservoir); Carnot engine $Q_H/T_H = Q_C/T_C$ |

drills.title: Convert km/h to m/s
drills.prompt: A car travels at {v} km/h. Express this speed in m/s (3 significant figures).
drills.solution:
$${v}\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{h}} \times \frac{1000\text{ m}}{1\text{ km}} \times \frac{1\text{ h}}{3600\text{ s}} = \frac{{v}}{3.6}\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$

So the speed is **{ms:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Convert an area from cm² to m²
drills.prompt: A solar cell has an area of {a} cm². What is its area in m²? (The conversion is exact, so give every digit.)
drills.solution:
$1\text{ cm} = 10^{-2}\text{ m}$, so $1\text{ cm}^2 = 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2$ (square the factor).

${a:dp0}\text{ cm}^2 \times 10^{-4}\,\tfrac{\text{m}^2}{\text{cm}^2} =$ **{m2:num4} m²**.

drills.title: Area with significant figures
drills.prompt: A rectangular sheet measures {l} m by {w} m. Find its area, rounded to the correct number of significant figures.
drills.solution: ${l} \times {w} = {A:num4}\text{ m}^2$. For a product, keep the fewest significant figures among the inputs: {l} has 3 and {w} has 2, so round to 2 significant figures: **{A:sig2} m²**.

drills.title: Components of a vector
drills.prompt: A force of {A} N points at {th}° measured counterclockwise from the $+x$ axis. Find its $x$ and $y$ components (include the signs), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$F_x = F\cos\theta = {A}\cos {th}^\circ =$ **{Ax:sig3} N**

$F_y = F\sin\theta = {A}\sin {th}^\circ =$ **{Ay:sig3} N**

The signs come out of the trig functions automatically when the angle is measured from $+x$.

drills.title: Add two displacement vectors
drills.prompt: A drone flies {a} km at {t1}° (counterclockwise from east), then {b} km at {t2}°. Find the magnitude of its total displacement and its direction in degrees counterclockwise from east (magnitude to 3 significant figures, direction to the nearest 0.1°).
drills.solution:
$R_x = {a}\cos {t1}^\circ + {b}\cos {t2}^\circ = {Rx:num2}$ km

$R_y = {a}\sin {t1}^\circ + {b}\sin {t2}^\circ = {Ry:num2}$ km

$R = \sqrt{R_x^2 + R_y^2} =$ **{R:sig3} km**, at $\theta =$ **{th:num1}°** (check the quadrant from the signs of $R_x$ and $R_y$).

drills.title: Angle between two vectors
drills.prompt: For $\vec A = {a1}\hat\imath {a2:signed}\hat\jmath {a3:signed}\hat k$ and $\vec B = {b1}\hat\imath {b2:signed}\hat\jmath {b3:signed}\hat k$, find $\vec A\cdot\vec B$ and the angle between the vectors in degrees (to the nearest 0.1°).

drills.title: Average velocity and average speed
drills.prompt: A jogger runs {d1} m east in {t1} s, then turns and runs {d2} m west in {t2} s. Find her average velocity (east positive) and her average speed for the whole run, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Displacement: $\Delta x = {d1} - {d2} = {dx}$ m; total time $\Delta t = {t1} + {t2} = {tt}$ s.

Average velocity $= \dfrac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} =$ **{vavg:sig3} m/s** (east).

Distance $= {d1} + {d2}$ m, so average speed $=$ **{savg:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Acceleration and displacement from a v–t graph
drills.prompt: A cart's velocity–time graph is a straight line from {v1} m/s at $t = 0$ to {v2} m/s at $t = {dur}$ s. Find its acceleration and its displacement over this interval, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The acceleration is the slope of the line: $a = \dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{{v2} - {v1}}{{dur}} =$ **{acc:sig3} m/s²**.

The displacement is the shaded area, a trapezoid: $\Delta x = \tfrac12({v1} + {v2})({dur}) =$ **{disp:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Braking distance and time
drills.prompt: A car moving at {v0} m/s brakes with a constant acceleration of magnitude {dec} m/s². How far does it travel while stopping, and how long does it take? Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
With $v = 0$ and $a = -{dec}$ m/s²: $0 = v_0^2 - 2({dec})\Delta x$, so $\Delta x = \dfrac{{v0}^2}{2({dec})} =$ **{d:sig3} m**.

$0 = {v0} - {dec}\,t$, so $t =$ **{t:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Time and speed of a dropped object
drills.prompt: A wrench is dropped from rest from a height of {h} m. Ignoring air resistance and using $g = 9.8$ m/s², how long does it fall, and how fast is it moving at the ground? Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$h = \tfrac12 g t^2 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{2({h})/9.8} =$ **{t:sig3} s**.

$v = gt = 9.8({t:sig3}) =$ **{v:sig3} m/s** (also $v = \sqrt{2gh}$).

drills.title: Ball thrown straight up
drills.prompt: A ball is thrown straight up at {v0} m/s. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its maximum height above the launch point and its total time in the air (until it returns to the launch height), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
At the top $v_y = 0$: $0 = {v0}^2 - 2(9.8)H$, so $H =$ **{H:sig3} m**.

Time up $= {v0}/9.8$ s; time down is the same, so $T = 2({v0})/9.8 =$ **{T:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Horizontal launch from a height
drills.prompt: A ball leaves the edge of a {h} m high ledge moving horizontally at {v} m/s. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², how far from the base of the ledge does it land, and what is its speed just before landing? Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Fall time from the vertical motion: $t = \sqrt{2h/g} = \sqrt{2({h})/9.8} = {t:sig3}$ s.

Horizontal distance: $x = v t = {v}({t:sig3}) =$ **{x:sig3} m**.

At impact $v_y = gt = {vy:num2}$ m/s, so speed $= \sqrt{{v}^2 + {vy:num2}^2} =$ **{s:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Range, height and flight time on level ground
drills.prompt: A ball is launched from level ground at {v0} m/s, {th}° above horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the time of flight, the maximum height and the range, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$v_{0x} = {v0}\cos {th}^\circ = {vx:num2}$ m/s, $v_{0y} = {v0}\sin {th}^\circ = {vy:num2}$ m/s.

$T = 2v_{0y}/g =$ **{T:sig3} s**; $H = v_{0y}^2/(2g) =$ **{H:sig3} m**; $R = v_{0x}T = \dfrac{v_0^2\sin 2\theta}{g} =$ **{R:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Crossing a river
drills.prompt: A river {w} m wide flows at {vc} m/s. A boat moves at {vs} m/s relative to the water. (a) Heading straight across, how far downstream does it land? (b) To land directly opposite, how many degrees upstream from straight across must it head? Give the drift to 3 significant figures and the angle to the nearest 0.1°.
drills.solution:
(a) Crossing time uses only the across component: $t = {w}/{vs} = {t:num2}$ s. Drift $= {vc} \times {t:num2} =$ **{drift:sig3} m**.

(b) The upstream component must cancel the current: ${vs}\sin\alpha = {vc}$, so $\alpha = \sin^{-1}({vc}/{vs}) =$ **{ang:num1}°**.

drills.title: Airplane in a crosswind
drills.prompt: A plane with airspeed {va} km/h must fly due north while a wind blows toward the east at {vw} km/h. How many degrees west of north must it head, and what is its ground speed? Give the heading to the nearest 0.1° and the ground speed to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\vec v_{PG} = \vec v_{PA} + \vec v_{AG}$. The plane's eastward airspeed component must be $-{vw}$ km/h: ${va}\sin\alpha = {vw}$, so $\alpha =$ **{head:num1}°** west of north.

Ground speed $= {va}\cos\alpha = \sqrt{{va}^2 - {vw}^2} =$ **{vg:sig3} km/h**.

drills.title: Average velocity and acceleration in two dimensions
drills.prompt: A boat starts at the origin and is at ({px} m, {py} m) {dur} s later. Over the same {dur} s its velocity changes from ({ux}, {uy}) m/s to ({wx}, {wy}) m/s. Find the magnitudes of its average velocity and its average acceleration, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Displacement $= ({px}, {py})$ m, of magnitude $\sqrt{({px})^2 + ({py})^2}$ m, so $|\vec v_{\text{avg}}| = \dfrac{|\Delta\vec r|}{\Delta t} =$ **{vav:sig3} m/s**.

$\Delta\vec v = ({wx} - ({ux}),\ {wy} - ({uy})) = ({dvx}, {dvy})$ m/s, so $|\vec a_{\text{avg}}| = \dfrac{\sqrt{({dvx})^2 + ({dvy})^2}}{{dur}} =$ **{aav:sig3} m/s²**. Subtract the velocity vectors component by component; the change in speed alone would miss any change in direction.

drills.title: Acceleration with an angled pull
drills.prompt: A {m} kg sled on frictionless ice is pulled by a rope with tension {F} N at {th}° above horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the sled's acceleration and the normal force on it. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Horizontal: ${F}\cos {th}^\circ = {m}a$, so $a =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

Vertical ($a_y = 0$): $n + {F}\sin {th}^\circ - {m}(9.8) = 0$, so $n =$ **{n:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Apparent weight in an elevator
drills.prompt: A {m} kg person stands on a scale in an elevator accelerating {dir} at {acc} m/s². What does the scale read? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s². Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The scale reads the normal force. With up positive, $n - mg = ma$, where $a = +{acc}$ m/s² if the acceleration is upward and $-{acc}$ m/s² if downward.

Acceleration is {dir}, so $a = {sa}$ m/s² and $n = m(g + a) = {m}(9.8 + ({sa})) =$ **{n:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Net force from two perpendicular forces
drills.prompt: Two horizontal forces act on a {m} kg puck on frictionless ice: {F1} N east and {F2} N north. Find the magnitude of its acceleration and its direction in degrees north of east. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$F_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{{F1}^2 + {F2}^2} = {Fn:num2}$ N, so $a = F_{\text{net}}/m = {Fn:num2}/{m} =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

Direction: $\tan^{-1}({F2}/{F1}) =$ **{ang:sig3}°** north of east (the acceleration points along the net force).

drills.title: Block on a frictionless incline
drills.prompt: A block is released from rest on a frictionless ramp inclined at {th}°. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its acceleration and its speed after sliding {L} m along the ramp. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Along the slope only $mg\sin\theta$ acts: $a = g\sin\theta = 9.8\sin {th}^\circ =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$v^2 = 2aL$, so $v = \sqrt{2({a:num2})({L})} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Sliding down an incline with friction
drills.prompt: A {m} kg block slides down a {th}° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is {mu}. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the friction force and the block's acceleration. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$n = mg\cos\theta = {m}(9.8)\cos {th}^\circ$, so $f_k = \mu_k n =$ **{f:sig3} N** (up the slope).

$a = g(\sin\theta - \mu_k\cos\theta) = 9.8(\sin {th}^\circ - {mu}\cos {th}^\circ) =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²** down the slope.

drills.title: Force needed to start a box moving
drills.prompt: A {m} kg box rests on a level floor with $\mu_s = {ms}$ and $\mu_k = {mk}$. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the smallest horizontal force that starts it moving, and its acceleration if that same force keeps pushing once it slides. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$n = mg = {m}(9.8)$ N. Maximum static friction: $\mu_s n =$ **{Fs:sig3} N**, the force needed to start it.

Sliding: $f_k = \mu_k n$, so $a = \dfrac{\mu_s n - \mu_k n}{\,m} = (\mu_s - \mu_k)g =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

drills.title: Atwood machine
drills.prompt: Masses of {m1} kg and {m2} kg hang on either side of an ideal pulley. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the magnitude of their acceleration and the tension in the rope. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Heavier side down: ${m1}g - T = {m1}a$ and $T - {m2}g = {m2}a$. Adding:

$a = \dfrac{{m1} - {m2}}{{m1} + {m2}}(9.8) =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$T = {m2}(g + a) = \dfrac{2m_1m_2}{m_1 + m_2}g =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Block on a table pulled by a hanging mass
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg block on a horizontal table ($\mu_k = {mu}$) is tied by a rope over an ideal pulley to a hanging {m2} kg mass. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the acceleration and the tension. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Table block: $T - \mu_k m_1 g = m_1 a$. Hanging mass: $m_2 g - T = m_2 a$. Adding:

$a = \dfrac{m_2 - \mu_k m_1}{m_1 + m_2}g = \dfrac{{m2} - ({mu})({m1})}{{m1} + {m2}}(9.8) =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$T = m_2(g - a) =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Tension in two symmetric cables
drills.prompt: A {m} kg sign hangs at rest from two cables, each making {th}° with the horizontal. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the tension in each cable. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Horizontal components cancel by symmetry. Vertically, $2T\sin\theta = mg$:

$T = \dfrac{{m}(9.8)}{2\sin {th}^\circ} =$ **{T:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Centripetal acceleration and force
drills.prompt: A {m} kg ball on a string moves in a horizontal circle of radius {r} m on a frictionless table, completing one revolution every {T} s. Find its speed, its centripetal acceleration and the string tension. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$v = 2\pi r/T = 2\pi({r})/{T} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

$a_c = v^2/r =$ **{ac:sig3} m/s²**, toward the center.

The string supplies the inward force: $T_{\text{string}} = ma_c =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Maximum speed on a flat curve
drills.prompt: What is the maximum speed at which a car can round a flat curve of radius {r} m if the coefficient of static friction between tires and road is {mu}? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s² and answer in m/s. Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Static friction supplies the inward force: $\mu_s mg = \dfrac{mv^2}{\,r}$, so

$v = \sqrt{\mu_s g r} = \sqrt{({mu})(9.8)({r})} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s** (about {kmh:num1} km/h). The mass cancels.

drills.title: Vertical loop
drills.prompt: A roller coaster loop has radius {r} m. (a) What minimum speed must a car have at the top to stay on the track? (b) A {m} kg rider passes the bottom at {vb} m/s; what normal force does the seat exert on her there? Use $g = 9.8$ m/s². Give answers to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) At the limit $n = 0$ and gravity alone gives the inward force: $mg = mv^2/r$, so $v_{\min} = \sqrt{gr} =$ **{vmin:sig3} m/s**.

(b) At the bottom the net force is upward: $n - mg = mv^2/r$, so $n = {m}(9.8) + \dfrac{{m}({vb})^2}{{r}} =$ **{n:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Work done by an angled force and by friction
drills.prompt: A crate is dragged {d} m across a level floor by a rope with tension {F} N at {th}° above horizontal. Kinetic friction on the crate is {f} N. Find the work done by the rope, the work done by friction (with its sign), and the net work, in joules to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Rope: $W = Fd\cos\theta = {F}({d})\cos {th}^\circ =$ **{WF:sig3} J**.

Friction opposes the motion ($\theta = 180^\circ$): $W = -{f}({d}) =$ **{Wf} J**.

Gravity and the normal force are perpendicular to the motion and do no work, so $W_{\text{net}} =$ **{Wnet:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Work–energy theorem
drills.prompt: A {m} kg cart moving at {v0} m/s is pushed {d} m by a constant net force of {F} N in its direction of motion. Use the work–energy theorem to find its final speed in m/s, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$W_{\text{net}} = Fd = {F}({d}) = {W:dp0}$ J $= \tfrac12mv_f^2 - \tfrac12mv_i^2$.

$v_f = \sqrt{v_i^2 + 2W/m} = \sqrt{{v0}^2 + 2({W:dp0})/{m}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Spring force and stored energy
drills.prompt: A spring with spring constant {k} N/m is stretched {xcm} cm from its natural length. What force does it exert (N), and how much work (J) was needed to stretch it? Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Hooke's law: $|F| = kx = {k:dp0}({x}) =$ **{F:sig3} N** (pulling back toward equilibrium).

Work = area under the $F$–$x$ line $= \tfrac12kx^2 = \tfrac12({k:dp0})({x})^2 =$ **{U:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Speed at the bottom of a ramp (with and without friction)
drills.prompt: A {m} kg box starts from rest at the top of a ramp {h} m high. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find (a) its speed at the bottom if the ramp is frictionless, and (b) its speed if friction removes {pct}% of its initial potential energy. Give speeds in m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) $mgh = \tfrac12mv^2$, so $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(9.8)({h})} =$ **{v0:sig3} m/s**.

(b) Friction removes {pct}% of $mgh$, so $\tfrac12mv^2 = (1 - {pct}/100)\,mgh$ and $v =$ **{v1:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Spring launcher
drills.prompt: A spring with $k = {k:dp0}$ N/m is compressed {xcm} cm and launches a {mg} g ball straight up. Ignoring air resistance and using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the ball's speed as it leaves the spring (neglect the small height change during launch) and the maximum height it reaches above the release point. Give the speed in m/s and the height in m, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Stored energy: $\tfrac12kx^2 = \tfrac12({k:dp0})({x})^2 = {U:num4}$ J.

Launch speed: $\tfrac12mv^2 = {U:num4}$ J with $m = {m}$ kg, so $v =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

Max height: $mgh = {U:num4}$ J, so $h = \dfrac{{U:num4}}{({m})(9.8)} =$ **{h:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Power to lift a load
drills.prompt: A motor lifts a {m} kg load {h} m at constant speed in {t} s. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the power delivered to the load and, if the motor is {eff}% efficient, the electrical power it draws, in watts to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Work against gravity: $mgh = {m:dp0}(9.8)({h})$ J. $P = \dfrac{mgh}{\,t} =$ **{P:sig3} W**.

Input: $P_{\text{in}} = P/\eta = P/{eff}\% =$ **{Pin:sig3} W**.

drills.title: Impulse and average force in a rebound
drills.prompt: A {mg} g ball hits a wall at {v1} m/s and rebounds straight back at {v2} m/s. The contact lasts {tms} ms. Find the magnitude of the impulse (N·s) and of the average force on the ball (N), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Rebound direction positive: $\Delta p = m(v_f - v_i) = {m}({v2} - (-{v1})) =$ **{J:sig3} N·s**.

$F_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{{J:num4}}{{tms}\times10^{-3}} =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Recoil (momentum from rest)
drills.prompt: A {M} kg person standing on frictionless ice throws a {m} kg package horizontally at {v} m/s. With what speed does the person recoil? Give m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Total momentum starts at zero and stays zero: ${m}({v}) + {M}V = 0$.

$|V| = \dfrac{{m}({v})}{{M}} =$ **{V:sig3} m/s**, opposite to the throw.

drills.title: Center of mass of three particles
drills.prompt: Find the center of mass of {m1} kg at $({x1}, {y1})$, {m2} kg at $({x2}, {y2})$ and {m3} kg at $({x3}, {y3})$ (coordinates in meters). Give each coordinate in meters to 2 decimal places.

drills.title: Perfectly inelastic collision
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg car moving at {v1} m/s collides with a {m2} kg car moving at {v2} m/s along the same line (negative means the opposite direction), and they lock together. Find their common velocity (m/s, with sign) and the kinetic energy lost (J), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Momentum: ${m1:dp0}({v1}) + {m2:dp0}({v2}) = ({m1:dp0} + {m2:dp0})v_f$, so $v_f =$ **{vf:sig3} m/s**.

$K_i = {Ki:dp0}$ J and $K_f = \tfrac12({Mt:dp0})v_f^2 = {Kf:dp0}$ J, so the loss is **{dK:int} J**.

drills.title: Elastic collision with a target at rest
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg cart moving at {v} m/s collides head-on and elastically with a {m2} kg cart at rest. Find both final velocities in m/s, to 3 significant figures (positive = original direction of motion).
drills.solution:
$v_{1f} = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i} = \dfrac{{m1} - {m2}}{{m1} + {m2}}({v}) =$ **{v1f:sig3} m/s**

$v_{2f} = \dfrac{2m_1}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i} =$ **{v2f:sig3} m/s**

Check: they separate at ${v2f:num2} - ({v1f:num2}) = {v}$ m/s, the same as the approach speed.

drills.title: Ballistic pendulum
drills.prompt: A {mg} g bullet embeds itself in a {M} kg block hanging from strings. The block swings up {hcm} cm. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the block's speed just after impact and the bullet's initial speed, in m/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Swing (energy conserved): $V = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(9.8)({hcm}/100)} =$ **{V:sig3} m/s**.

Collision (momentum conserved): $mv = (m + M)V$, so $v = \dfrac{{m:dp3} + {M}}{{m:dp3}}({V:num4}) =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Spinning down with constant angular acceleration
drills.prompt: A wheel spinning at {rpm} rpm slows uniformly to rest in {t} s. Find its angular acceleration (rad/s², with sign) and the number of revolutions it makes while stopping, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega_0 = {rpm:dp0}\times\dfrac{2\pi}{60} = {w0:num2}$ rad/s.

$\alpha = \dfrac{0 - \omega_0}{\,t} =$ **{alpha:sig3} rad/s²**.

$\Delta\theta = \tfrac12(\omega_0 + 0)t = {th:dp1}$ rad $=$ **{rev:sig3} rev**.

drills.title: Moment of inertia of masses on a rod
drills.prompt: A uniform rod of mass {M} kg and length {L} m has a small {m1} kg mass at its left end and a {m2} kg mass at its right end. Find the moment of inertia about (a) a perpendicular axis through the rod's center and (b) a perpendicular axis through the left end. Give kg·m² to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) Rod: $\tfrac1{12}ML^2$; each end mass is $L/2$ away: $I = \tfrac1{12}({M})({L})^2 + ({m1} + {m2})({L}/2)^2 =$ **{Ic:sig3} kg·m²**.

(b) Rod about an end: $\tfrac13ML^2$; the left mass is on the axis, the right mass is $L$ away: $I = \tfrac13({M})({L})^2 + {m2}({L})^2 =$ **{Ie:sig3} kg·m²**.

drills.title: Rotational kinetic energy of a disk
drills.prompt: A {M} kg {shape} of radius {R} m spins about its central axis at {rpm} rpm. Find its moment of inertia (kg·m²) and its rotational kinetic energy (J), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
For a {shape}, $I = cMR^2$ with $c = {shape:num1}$, so $I =$ **{I:sig3} kg·m²**.

$\omega = {rpm:dp0}\times\dfrac{2\pi}{60} = {w:num2}$ rad/s, so $K = \tfrac12I\omega^2 =$ **{K:sig3} J**.

drills.title: Torque from an angled force
drills.prompt: A force of {F} N is applied at the end of a {r} m wrench, making an angle of {th}° with the handle. Find the torque about the bolt, and the maximum torque that force could produce, in N·m to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\tau = rF\sin\theta = ({r})({F})\sin {th}^\circ =$ **{tau:sig3} N·m**.

The maximum occurs for a perpendicular push: $rF =$ **{tmax:sig3} N·m**.

drills.title: Mass hanging from a heavy pulley
drills.prompt: A {m} kg block hangs from a light rope wrapped around a {M} kg solid cylinder of radius {R} m that turns freely on a frictionless axle. The block is released. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the block's acceleration (m/s²), the rope tension (N) and the cylinder's angular acceleration (rad/s²), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Block: $mg - T = ma$. Cylinder: $TR = \tfrac12MR^2\alpha$ with $\alpha = a/R$, so $T = \tfrac12Ma$.

$a = \dfrac{mg}{m + \tfrac12M} = \dfrac{{m}(9.8)}{{m} + {M}/2} =$ **{a:sig3} m/s²**.

$T = \tfrac12({M})({a:num2}) =$ **{T:sig3} N**; $\alpha = a/R =$ **{alpha:sig3} rad/s²**.

drills.title: Rolling down a ramp
drills.prompt: A {shape} rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp, dropping a height of {h} m. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find its speed at the bottom in m/s, to 3 significant figures. (For comparison, a frictionless sliding block would reach {vs:num2} m/s.)
drills.solution:
With $I = cMR^2$ and $\omega = v/R$: $Mgh = \tfrac12Mv^2 + \tfrac12cMv^2 = \tfrac12(1 + c)Mv^2$, and for a {shape} $c = {shape:num4}$.

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{1 + c}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2(9.8)({h})}{1 + {shape:num4}}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Conservation of angular momentum
drills.prompt: A skater spins at {f} rev/s with moment of inertia {I1} kg·m². She pulls in her arms, reducing her moment of inertia to {pct}% of its original value. Find her new spin rate (rev/s) and her new rotational kinetic energy (J), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
No external torque: $I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$, so $f_2 = f_1\dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = \dfrac{{f}}{{pct}/100} =$ **{f2:sig3} rev/s**.

New $I_2 = {I2:num2}$ kg·m² and $\omega_2 = 2\pi f_2$; $K_2 = \tfrac12I_2\omega_2^2 =$ **{K2:sig3} J** (up from {K1:num1} J; her muscles did the work).

drills.title: Balancing a seesaw
drills.prompt: A uniform seesaw is pivoted at its center. A {m1} kg person sits {d1} m from the pivot. How far from the pivot, on the other side, must a {m2} kg person sit to balance it? Give meters to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Torques about the pivot must cancel (the seesaw's weight and the pivot force act at the pivot): ${m1}g({d1}) = {m2}g\,x$.

$x = \dfrac{{m1}({d1})}{{m2}} =$ **{d2:sig3} m**.

drills.title: Beam on two supports
drills.prompt: A uniform {L} m beam of mass {mb} kg rests on supports at its ends A and B. A {m} kg crate sits {x:num2} m from end A. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the upward force from each support, in newtons to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Torques about A: $F_B({L}) = {mb}(9.8)({L}/2) + {m}(9.8)({x:num2})$, so $F_B =$ **{FB:sig3} N**.

Vertical forces: $F_A = ({mb} + {m})(9.8) - F_B =$ **{FA:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Stress and stretch of a hanging wire
drills.prompt: A {len:num1} m long {mat} wire with a diameter of {dia:num1} mm hangs vertically with a {mass} kg mass at its lower end. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the tensile stress in the wire (Pa) and how much the wire stretches (mm), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The radius is half the diameter, so $A = \pi r^2 = \pi\left(\dfrac{{dia:num1}}{2}\times10^{-3}\right)^2 = {Aw:texsci}$ m². The tension equals the weight, $mg = {mass}(9.8) = {Fw:num1}$ N.

Stress $= \dfrac{F}{A} = \dfrac{{Fw:num1}}{{Aw:texsci}} = \mathbf{{stress:texsci}}$ Pa.

Strain $=$ stress$/Y$, and $\Delta L = \text{strain}\times L_0 = \dfrac{({stress:texsci})({len:num1})}{{mat:texsci}} = {dLm:texsci}$ m $=$ **{dLmm:sig3} mm**.

drills.title: Shear deformation of a pad
drills.prompt: A rubber pad {thick} cm thick has a square top face {side} cm on a side and a shear modulus of {shmod}. Its bottom is fixed, and a sideways force of {force:dp0} N acts along its top face. Find the shear stress (Pa) and how far the top face shifts sideways (mm), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The force lies along the top face, a square {side} cm $= {sidem:num2}$ m on a side, so $A = ({sidem:num2})^2 = {Ar:num4}$ m².

Shear stress $= \dfrac{F}{A} = \dfrac{{force:dp0}}{{Ar:num4}} =$ **{tau:sig3} Pa**.

$\Delta x = \dfrac{F L_0}{SA} = \dfrac{({force:dp0})({thick}/100)}{({shmod:texsci})({Ar:num4})} =$ **{dxmm:sig3} mm**.

drills.title: Bulk compression under water

choices.label: sealed flexible bag of water ($B = 2.2\times10^{9}$ Pa)

drills.prompt: A {vol:num1} L {mat} is lowered to a depth of {depth:dp0} m in water of density 1000 kg/m³. Ignoring the atmosphere and using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the increase in pressure on it (Pa) and how much its volume decreases (cm³), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\Delta P = \rho g h = (1000)(9.8)({depth:dp0}) = \mathbf{{dP:texsci}}$ Pa.

From $\Delta P = -B\,\Delta V/V_0$, the volume decrease is $|\Delta V| = V_0\dfrac{\Delta P}{B} = ({vol:num1}\times1000\text{ cm}^3)\dfrac{{dP:texsci}}{{mat:texsci}} =$ **{dV:sig3} cm³**.

drills.title: Gravitational force and surface gravity
drills.prompt: A planet has mass ${Mm}\times10^{{Me}}$ kg and radius ${Rm}\times10^{6}$ m. Using $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg², find the acceleration due to gravity at its surface (m/s²) and the weight there of a {m} kg probe (N), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2} = \dfrac{(6.67\times10^{-11})({Mm}\times10^{{Me}})}{({Rm}\times10^{6})^2} =$ **{gs:sig3} m/s²**.

Weight $= mg = {m}({gs:num2}) =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

drills.title: Circular orbit speed and period
drills.prompt: A satellite is in a circular orbit {h} km above Earth's surface. Using $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg², $M_E = 5.97\times10^{24}$ kg and $R_E = 6.37\times10^{6}$ m, find its orbital speed (m/s) and period (minutes), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Orbit radius from Earth's center: $r = R_E + h = {r:texsci}$ m.

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM_E}{\,r}} =$ **{v:sig3} m/s**.

$T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{\,v} =$ **{T:sig3} min**.

drills.title: Escape speed
drills.prompt: Find the escape speed (km/s) from the surface of a planet with mass ${Mm}\times10^{{Me}}$ kg and radius ${Rm}\times10^{6}$ m, and the speed of a circular orbit just above its surface. Use $G = 6.67\times10^{-11}$ N·m²/kg² and give both speeds in km/s to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Total energy zero: $\tfrac12mv^2 = \dfrac{GMm}{\,R}$, so $v_{\text{esc}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{\,R}} =$ **{ve:sig3} km/s**.

Low orbit: $v = \sqrt{GM/R} = v_{\text{esc}}/\sqrt2 =$ **{vo:sig3} km/s**.

drills.title: Period and frequency of a mass on a spring
drills.prompt: A {m} kg block on a frictionless surface is attached to a spring with $k = {k:dp0}$ N/m. Find the period (s) and the frequency (Hz) of its oscillation, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega = \sqrt{k/m} = \sqrt{{k:dp0}/{m}} = {w:num2}$ rad/s.

$T = 2\pi/\omega = 2\pi\sqrt{m/k} =$ **{T:sig3} s**, and $f = 1/T =$ **{f:sig3} Hz**.

drills.title: Simple pendulum
drills.prompt: A simple pendulum {L} m long swings with small amplitude on {planet}. Find its period in seconds, to 3 significant figures. (Use $g = 9.8$ m/s² on Earth, 1.62 m/s² on the Moon, 3.71 m/s² on Mars.)
drills.solution: $T = 2\pi\sqrt{L/g} = 2\pi\sqrt{{L}/{planet:num2}} =$ **{T:sig3} s**. The bob's mass doesn't matter.

drills.title: Maximum speed and acceleration in SHM
drills.prompt: A {m} kg mass on a spring ($k = {k:dp0}$ N/m) oscillates with amplitude {Acm} cm. Find its maximum speed, its maximum acceleration, and its speed when it is {x:num4} m from equilibrium. Use m/s and m/s², to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\omega = \sqrt{k/m} = {w:num4}$ rad/s.

$v_{\max} = A\omega = ({A})({w:num4}) =$ **{vmax:sig3} m/s**; $a_{\max} = A\omega^2 =$ **{amax:sig3} m/s²**.

From energy, $v = \omega\sqrt{A^2 - x^2} = {w:num4}\sqrt{{A}^2 - {x:num4}^2} =$ **{vx:sig3} m/s**.

drills.title: Wave speed, frequency and wavelength
drills.prompt: A {f} Hz tone travels as {kind} (speed {kind:int} m/s). Find its wavelength (m) and its period (s), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\lambda = v/f = {kind:dp0}/{f:dp0} =$ **{lam:sig3} m**.

$T = 1/f = 1/{f:dp0} = \mathbf{{T:texsci}}$ s.

drills.title: Harmonics of a stretched string
drills.prompt: A string {L} m long with mass {mg} g is fixed at both ends under {F} N of tension. Find the wave speed, the fundamental frequency and the frequency of harmonic $n = {n}$, to 3 significant figures (m/s and Hz).

drills.title: Intensity and decibels
drills.prompt: A small speaker radiates {P} W of sound equally in all directions. At {r} m away, find the intensity (W/m², to 3 significant figures) and the sound intensity level (dB, to 1 decimal place). Use $I_0 = 10^{-12}$ W/m².
drills.solution:
$I = \dfrac{\,P}{4\pi r^2} = \dfrac{{P}}{4\pi({r})^2} = \mathbf{{I:texsci}}$ W/m².

$\beta = 10\log_{10}\dfrac{\,I}{I_0} =$ **{B:num1} dB**.

drills.title: Doppler shift from a moving source
drills.prompt: A siren emits {f} Hz and moves at {vs} m/s past a stationary listener. Using $v = 343$ m/s, find the frequency heard as it approaches and as it recedes, in Hz to 4 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Approaching source: $f' = f\dfrac{v}{v - v_s} = {f:dp0}\cdot\dfrac{343}{343 - {vs}} =$ **{fa:sig4} Hz**.

Receding: $f' = {f:dp0}\cdot\dfrac{343}{343 + {vs}} =$ **{fr:sig4} Hz**.

drills.title: Resonances of an air column
drills.prompt: A pipe {L} m long is {pipe}. Using $v = 343$ m/s, find its fundamental frequency and the next higher resonant frequency, in Hz to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Open at both ends: $f_n = nv/(2L)$, all $n$. Closed at one end: $f_n = nv/(4L)$, odd $n$ only. This pipe is {pipe}.

$f_1 =$ **{f1:sig3} Hz**, and the next resonance is **{f2:sig3} Hz** ($2f_1$ for an open pipe, $3f_1$ for a closed one).

drills.title: Beats
drills.prompt: Two tuning forks of {f1} Hz and {f2} Hz are struck together. Find the beat frequency and the frequency of the tone you hear throbbing, in Hz (the tone to 1 decimal place).
drills.solution:
$f_{\text{beat}} = |f_1 - f_2| = |{f1} - {f2}| =$ **{fb} Hz**.

The tone heard is the average frequency, $\tfrac12({f1} + {f2}) =$ **{favg:num1} Hz**, getting louder and softer {fb} times per second.

drills.title: Pressure at depth
drills.prompt: Find the gauge pressure and the absolute pressure {h} m below the surface of {fluid}. Use $g = 9.8$ m/s² and $P_{\text{atm}} = 1.013\times10^5$ Pa, and give both in pascals to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Gauge: $\rho gh = ({fluid:dp0})(9.8)({h}) = \mathbf{{Pg:texsci}}$ Pa.

Absolute: $P_{\text{atm}} + \rho gh = \mathbf{{Pabs:texsci}}$ Pa, about {natm:num2} atm.

drills.title: Apparent weight and floating fraction
drills.prompt: An object of density {rho:dp0} kg/m³ and volume {Vc:dp0} cm³ is held completely under water (density 1000 kg/m³). Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the buoyant force and its apparent weight (weight minus buoyant force; a negative value means it would float up if released), both in newtons to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$V = {Vc:dp0}\text{ cm}^3 = {V:texsci}$ m³. $F_B = \rho_{\text{water}}Vg = 1000({V:texsci})(9.8) =$ **{FB:num2} N**.

Weight $= \rho Vg = {W:num2}$ N, so weight minus buoyancy $=$ **{app:num2} N**. A positive value is the force you must hold it up with; a negative value means it is less dense than water and you must push it down.

drills.title: Hydraulic lift
drills.prompt: A hydraulic lift has pistons of diameter {d1} cm and {d2} cm. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², what force on the small piston supports a {m} kg car on the large one, and how far must the small piston move in total to raise the car {h} m? Give the force in newtons and the distance in meters, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Area ratio $= (d_2/d_1)^2 = ({d2}/{d1})^2 = {ratio:sig4}$.

Pascal: $F_1 = \dfrac{mg}{A_2/A_1} = \dfrac{{m:dp0}(9.8)}{{ratio:sig4}} =$ **{F1:num1} N**.

Equal volumes: $d_1 = {h}({ratio:sig4}) =$ **{s1:num1} m** (many pump strokes).

drills.title: Continuity equation
drills.prompt: Water flows at {v1} m/s through a pipe of diameter {D1} cm that narrows to {D2} cm. Find the speed in the narrow section (m/s) and the flow rate in liters per second, to 3 significant figures.

drills.title: Pressure in a narrowing horizontal pipe
drills.prompt: Water flows through a horizontal pipe. Where the pressure is {P1k} kPa the speed is {v1} m/s. At a narrower section the speed is {v2} m/s. What is the pressure there, in kPa to 3 significant figures? (Water density 1000 kg/m³.)
drills.solution:
Same height, so $P_1 + \tfrac12\rho v_1^2 = P_2 + \tfrac12\rho v_2^2$:

$P_2 = {P1k}\times10^3 + \tfrac12(1000)({v1}^2 - {v2}^2) = {P2:int}$ Pa $=$ **{P2k:num2} kPa**. Faster flow, lower pressure.

drills.title: Draining tank (Torricelli)
drills.prompt: A large open tank has a hole of area {a} cm² located {h} m below the water surface. Using $g = 9.8$ m/s², find the speed of the emerging water (m/s) and the initial flow rate in L/s, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Torricelli: $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2(9.8)({h})} =$ **{v:num2} m/s**.

$Q = Av = ({a}\times10^{-4})({v:num2})$ m³/s $=$ **{Q:num2} L/s**.

drills.title: Final temperature of a mixture
drills.prompt: A {m1} kg block of {metal} ($c = {metal:dp0}$ J/(kg·K)) at {T1}°C is dropped into {m2} kg of water ($c = 4186$ J/(kg·K)) at {T2}°C in an insulated cup. Ignoring the cup, find the final temperature in °C, to the nearest 0.1°C.

drills.title: Heat to melt and warm ice
drills.prompt: How much heat is needed to turn {m} kg of ice at {Ti}°C into water at {Tf}°C? Use $c_{\text{ice}} = 2100$ J/(kg·K), $L_f = 3.34\times10^5$ J/kg and $c_{\text{water}} = 4186$ J/(kg·K), and give the answer in joules to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Warm the ice to 0°C: ${m}(2100)(0 - ({Ti})) = {Q1:dp0}$ J.

Melt it: ${m}(3.34\times10^5) = {Q2:dp0}$ J.

Warm the water: ${m}(4186)({Tf}) = {Q3:dp0}$ J.

Total: $Q = \mathbf{{Q:texsci}}$ J.

drills.title: Thermal expansion
drills.prompt: A {L} m long piece of {mat} warms from {T1}°C to {T2}°C. By how many millimeters does it lengthen? Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $\Delta L = \alpha L\Delta T = ({mat}\times10^{-6})({L})({T2} - ({T1})) =$ **{dL:num2} mm**. (A Celsius difference equals a kelvin difference.)

drills.title: Heat conduction through a wall
drills.prompt: A {A} m² panel of {k} is {Lcm} cm thick. The temperature difference across it is {dT} K. Find the rate of heat conduction (W) and the heat lost in one hour (kJ), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\dfrac{Q}{t} = \dfrac{kA\Delta T}{L} = \dfrac{({k:num2})({A})({dT})}{{Lcm}/100} =$ **{P:num1} W**.

In 3600 s: **{E:num1} kJ**.

drills.title: Ideal gas law
drills.prompt: {n} mol of an ideal gas at {TC}°C occupies {VL} L. What is its pressure, in pascals to 3 significant figures? ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K))
drills.solution:
Convert: $T = {TC} + 273.15 = {T:num2}$ K, $V = {VL}\times10^{-3}$ m³.

$P = \dfrac{nRT}{V} = \dfrac{({n})(8.314)({T:num2})}{{VL}\times10^{-3}} = \mathbf{{P:texsci}}$ Pa.

drills.title: Combined gas law
drills.prompt: A gas occupies {V1} L at {P1} atm and {T1} K. What volume does it occupy at {P2} atm and {T2} K? Give liters to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $\dfrac{P_1V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$, so $V_2 = V_1\cdot\dfrac{P_1}{P_2}\cdot\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = {V1}\cdot\dfrac{{P1}}{{P2}}\cdot\dfrac{{T2}}{{T1}} =$ **{V2:num2} L**.

drills.title: RMS speed and average kinetic energy
drills.prompt: Find the rms speed of {gas} molecules at {T} K (m/s) and their average translational kinetic energy (J), to 3 significant figures. ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K), $k_B = 1.38\times10^{-23}$ J/K)
drills.solution:
$v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3(8.314)({T:dp0})}{{gas:sig3}}} =$ **{v:int} m/s** ($M$ in kg/mol).

$\overline K = \tfrac32k_BT = \mathbf{{K:texsci}}$ J (the same for every gas at this temperature).

drills.title: First law of thermodynamics
drills.prompt: During a process a gas absorbs {Q} J of heat (negative means it releases heat) and does {W} J of work on its surroundings (negative means work is done on it). Find the change in its internal energy, in joules.
drills.solution: $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = Q - W = ({Q}) - ({W}) =$ **{dU} J**, with $Q$ into the gas and $W$ done by the gas.

drills.title: Constant-pressure process for a monatomic gas
drills.prompt: {n} mol of a monatomic ideal gas is heated at constant pressure, raising its temperature by {dT} K. Find the work done by the gas, the change in internal energy, and the heat added, in joules to 3 significant figures. ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K))
drills.solution:
$W = P\Delta V = nR\Delta T = ({n})(8.314)({dT}) =$ **{W:num1} J**.

$\Delta E_{\text{int}} = \tfrac32nR\Delta T =$ **{dU:num1} J**.

$Q = \Delta E_{\text{int}} + W = \tfrac52nR\Delta T =$ **{Q:num1} J**.

drills.title: Isothermal expansion
drills.prompt: {n} mol of an ideal gas expands isothermally at {T} K until its volume is {r} times larger. How much work does it do, and how much heat does it absorb? Give joules to 3 significant figures. ($R = 8.314$ J/(mol·K), and the work in an isothermal process is $nRT\ln(V_f/V_i)$.)
drills.solution:
The work is the area under the isotherm on a PV diagram, $W = nRT\ln\dfrac{V_f}{V_i} = ({n})(8.314)({T})\ln {r} =$ **{W:num1} J**.

Isothermal: $\Delta E_{\text{int}} = 0$, so $Q = W =$ **{W:num1} J**.

drills.title: Carnot efficiency and heat rejected
drills.prompt: An ideal (Carnot) engine runs between a hot reservoir at {TH}°C and a cold one at {TC}°C. Find its efficiency (as a decimal) and, if it absorbs {QH} J per cycle, the work output and the heat rejected per cycle, in joules. Give all three to 3 significant figures, and convert with $T = T_C + 273$.
drills.solution:
In kelvins, $T_H = {TH} + 273$ and $T_C = {TC} + 273$. $e = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H} =$ **{e:num4}**.

$W = eQ_H =$ **{W:num1} J**; $Q_C = Q_H - W =$ **{QC:num1} J**.

drills.title: Engine efficiency from work and exhaust heat
drills.prompt: An engine does {W} J of work per cycle and exhausts {QC} J of heat. How much heat does it absorb per cycle (J), and what is its efficiency (as a decimal to 3 significant figures)?
drills.solution:
First law over a cycle: $Q_H = W + Q_C = {W:dp0} + {QC:dp0} =$ **{QH:dp0} J**.

$e = W/Q_H =$ **{e:num4}**.

drills.title: Entropy change when ice melts in a warm room
drills.prompt: {m} kg of ice at 0°C melts, taking all its heat from a large room at {Tr}°C. Find the entropy change of (a) the ice and (b) the room, and (c) the total, in J/K to 3 significant figures (keep at least 4 significant figures in intermediate steps). ($L_f = 3.34\times10^5$ J/kg; use $T = T_C + 273.15$.)
drills.solution:
Heat: $Q = mL_f = {m}(3.34\times10^5) = {Qh:dp0}$ J.

(a) The ice absorbs it at 273.15 K: $\Delta S = \dfrac{Q}{T} = \dfrac{{Qh:dp0}}{273.15} =$ **{S1:num1} J/K**.

(b) The room gives up the same heat at ${Troom:num2}$ K: $\Delta S = -\dfrac{{Qh:dp0}}{{Troom:num2}} =$ **{S2:num1} J/K**.

(c) Total: **{Stot:num2} J/K**, positive because heat flowed from hot to cold.

drills.title: Coulomb force between two charges
drills.prompt: Charges of {Q1} μC and {Q2} μC are {rcm} cm apart. Find the magnitude of the electric force between them, in newtons to 3 significant figures ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²). Is it attractive or repulsive?
drills.solution:
$F = k\dfrac{|q_1q_2|}{r^2} = (8.99\times10^9)\dfrac{({q1}\times10^{-6})({q2}\times10^{-6})}{({r})^2} =$ **{F:sig3} N**.

It is repulsive if the signs match and attractive if they differ.

drills.title: Net force from two charges on a line
drills.prompt: A charge of $+{qa}$ μC is at $x = 0$ and a charge of ${qb}$ μC is at $x = {d}$ cm. Find the net force on a $+1.0$ μC charge at $x = {x}$ cm, as a signed $x$ component in newtons to 3 significant figures ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²).
drills.solution:
From the charge at 0 (it repels the test charge toward $+x$): $F_{1x} = +k\dfrac{({qa}\times10^{-6})(1.0\times10^{-6})}{({x}/100)^2} = {FA:num2}$ N.

From the charge at {d} cm: $F_{2x} = -k\dfrac{({qb}\times10^{-6})(1.0\times10^{-6})}{(({d} - {x})/100)^2} = {FB:num2}$ N (a positive charge there pushes toward $-x$; a negative one pulls toward $+x$).

Net: $F_x = F_{1x} + F_{2x} =$ **{Fnet:num2} N**.

drills.title: Field and force from a point charge
drills.prompt: Find the electric field {rcm} cm from a $+{q}$ nC point charge, and the magnitude of the force on a $-{qt}$ μC charge placed there, in N/C and N to 3 significant figures ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²).
drills.solution:
$E = k\dfrac{\,q}{r^2} = (8.99\times10^9)\dfrac{{q}\times10^{-9}}{({r})^2} =$ **{E:num1} N/C**, pointing away from the positive charge.

$F = |q_t|E = ({qt}\times10^{-6})({E:dp1}) =$ **{F:sig3} N**, toward the source charge (a negative charge is pushed against $\vec E$).

drills.title: Charged particle in a uniform field
drills.prompt: Starting from rest, {part} is in a uniform electric field of {E:dp0} N/C. Find its acceleration (m/s²) and its speed (m/s) after it travels {dcm} cm, to 3 significant figures. ($e = 1.602\times10^{-19}$ C, $m_e = 9.11\times10^{-31}$ kg, $m_p = 1.673\times10^{-27}$ kg)
drills.solution:
$a = \dfrac{eE}{m} = \dfrac{(1.602\times10^{-19})({E:dp0})}{{part:texsci}} = \mathbf{{a:texsci}}$ m/s².

$v = \sqrt{2ad} = \mathbf{{v:texsci}}$ m/s.

drills.title: Field between two charges
drills.prompt: A $+{q1}$ nC charge is at $x = 0$ and a ${q2}$ nC charge is at $x = {d}$ cm. Find the $x$ component of the electric field at the midpoint, in kN/C to 3 significant figures (positive = toward the second charge).
drills.solution:
Each charge is ${d}/2$ cm from the midpoint. The first charge's field there points away from it, in $+x$: $E_{1x} = k({q1}\times10^{-9})/r^2 = {E1:dp1}$ N/C.

A positive second charge makes a field pointing away from it ($-x$); a negative one, toward it ($+x$). So $E_{2x} = -k({q2}\times10^{-9})/r^2 = -({E2:dp1})$ N/C.

$E_x = E_{1x} + E_{2x} =$ **{E:num2} kN/C**.

drills.title: Field inside and outside a charged sphere
drills.prompt: A solid insulating sphere of radius {Rcm} cm carries $+{Q}$ nC spread uniformly through its volume. Find the field at {rincm:num1} cm and at {routcm:num1} cm from its center, in N/C to 3 significant figures ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²).
drills.solution:
Inside, a Gaussian sphere of radius $r$ encloses $Q(r/R)^3$, so $E = \dfrac{kQr}{R^3} = \dfrac{(8.99\times10^9)({Q}\times10^{-9})({rin:num4})}{({R})^3} =$ **{Ein:num1} N/C**.

Outside it acts like a point charge: $E = \dfrac{kQ}{r^2} = \dfrac{(8.99\times10^9)({Q}\times10^{-9})}{({rout:num4})^2} =$ **{Eout:num1} N/C**.

drills.title: Field of a long line charge
drills.prompt: A long straight wire carries a uniform charge of {lam} nC per meter. Using Gauss's law, find the electric field {rcm} cm from the wire, in N/C to 3 significant figures ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²).
drills.solution:
A coaxial Gaussian cylinder gives $E(2\pi rL) = \lambda L/\varepsilon_0$, so $E = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0r} = \dfrac{2k\lambda}{r}$.

$E = \dfrac{2(8.99\times10^9)({lam}\times10^{-9})}{{rcm}/100} =$ **{E:int} N/C**.

drills.title: Potential from two charges and work to bring in a third
drills.prompt: Point P is {a} cm from a {q1} nC charge and {b} cm from a {q2} nC charge. Find the potential at P (zero at infinity) and the work needed to bring a $+{q3}$ nC charge from infinity to P, in μJ. Give both to 3 significant figures ($k = 8.99\times10^9$ N·m²/C²).
drills.solution:
Potentials add as signed scalars: $V = k\left(\dfrac{q_1}{r_1} + \dfrac{q_2}{r_2}\right) = (8.99\times10^9)\left(\dfrac{{q1}\times10^{-9}}{{a}/100} + \dfrac{{q2}\times10^{-9}}{{b}/100}\right) =$ **{V:num1} V**.

Work $= q\Delta V = ({q3}\times10^{-9})({V:dp1}) = {W:texsci}$ J $=$ **{Wu:sig3} μJ**.

drills.title: Speed after acceleration through a potential difference
drills.prompt: Starting from rest, {part} is accelerated through a potential difference of {dV:dp0} V. Find its kinetic energy in joules and its final speed in m/s, to 3 significant figures. ($e = 1.602\times10^{-19}$ C, $m_e = 9.11\times10^{-31}$ kg, $m_p = 1.673\times10^{-27}$ kg)
drills.solution:
$K = e\Delta V = {dV:dp0}$ eV $= (1.602\times10^{-19})({dV:dp0}) = \mathbf{{K:texsci}}$ J.

$v = \sqrt{2K/m} = \mathbf{{v:texsci}}$ m/s.

drills.title: Uniform field between plates
drills.prompt: Two parallel plates {dmm} mm apart are held at a potential difference of {V} V. Find the field between them (V/m) and the force on a {qn} nC charge there (N), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$E = \dfrac{\Delta V}{d} = \dfrac{{V}}{{dmm}\times10^{-3}} =$ **{E:int} V/m**.

$F = qE = ({qn}\times10^{-9})({E:dp0}) = \mathbf{{F:texsci}}$ N.

drills.title: Parallel-plate capacitor
drills.prompt: A parallel-plate capacitor has square plates {side} cm on a side, {dmm} mm apart, filled with {kap}. Find its capacitance in pF and the charge in nC when it is connected to {V} V, to 3 significant figures. ($\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}$ F/m)
drills.solution:
$A = ({side}/100)^2 = {A:num4}$ m². $C = \kappa\dfrac{\varepsilon_0A}{d} = {kap:num2}\cdot\dfrac{(8.85\times10^{-12})({A:num4})}{{dmm}\times10^{-3}} =$ **{C:num1} pF**.

$Q = CV =$ **{Q:num2} nC**.

drills.title: Capacitors in series and parallel
drills.prompt: Capacitors $C_2 = {C2}$ μF and $C_3 = {C3}$ μF are in parallel, and that pair is in series with $C_1 = {C1}$ μF. The combination is connected to {V} V. Find the equivalent capacitance (μF), the charge on $C_1$ (μC), and the voltage across $C_1$ (V), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Parallel pair: ${C2} + {C3} = {Cp}$ μF. In series with $C_1$: $C_{\text{eq}} = \dfrac{({C1})({Cp})}{{C1} + {Cp}} =$ **{Ceq:num2} μF**.

Series parts share the same charge: $Q = C_{\text{eq}}V =$ **{Q:num1} μC**.

$V_1 = Q/C_1 =$ **{V1:num2} V** (the remaining {V} − {V1:num2} V is across the parallel pair).

drills.title: Energy stored in a capacitor
drills.prompt: A {C} μF capacitor is charged to {V:dp0} V and then discharged in {tms} ms. Find the stored energy (J) and the average power during discharge (W), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$U = \tfrac12CV^2 = \tfrac12({C}\times10^{-6})({V:dp0})^2 =$ **{U:sig3} J**.

$\bar P = U/t =$ **{P:sig3} W**.

drills.title: Ohm's law and power
drills.prompt: A {V} V source is connected across a {R:dp0} Ω resistor. Find the current (A) and the power dissipated (W), to 3 significant figures.

drills.title: Resistance of a wire
drills.prompt: A {mat} wire is {L} m long with a diameter of {dmm} mm. Find its resistance (Ω) and the voltage drop across it (V) when it carries {I} A, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$A = \pi r^2 = \pi\left(\dfrac{{dmm}\times10^{-3}}{2}\right)^2 = {A:texsci}$ m².

$R = \rho\dfrac{\,L}{\,A} = ({mat:num2}\times10^{-8})\dfrac{{L}}{{A:texsci}} =$ **{R:sig3} Ω**.

$V = IR =$ **{V:sig3} V**.

drills.title: Cost of running an appliance
drills.prompt: An appliance rated {P:dp0} W runs {h} hours a day for {days} days. Electricity costs {rate:money} per kWh. How many kWh does it use (3 significant figures), and what does it cost (to the nearest cent)?
drills.solution:
Energy $= P\times t = ({P:dp0}/1000\text{ kW})({h}\text{ h/day})({days}\text{ days}) =$ **{E:num2} kWh**.

Cost $= {E:num4} \times {rate} =$ **{cost:money}**.

drills.title: Series–parallel resistor network
drills.prompt: A {R1} Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of {R2} Ω and {R3} Ω, all connected to an ideal {V} V battery. Find the equivalent resistance (Ω), the battery current (A), and the current through the {R2} Ω resistor (A), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Parallel pair: $\dfrac{({R2})({R3})}{{R2} + {R3}} = {Rp:num2}$ Ω; total $R_{\text{eq}} = {R1} + {Rp:num2} =$ **{Req:num2} Ω**.

$I = V/R_{\text{eq}} =$ **{I:num4} A**. Voltage across the pair: $IR_p = {Vp:num2}$ V.

Current in the {R2} Ω resistor: ${Vp:num2}/{R2} =$ **{I2:num4} A**.

drills.title: EMF and internal resistance
drills.prompt: A battery with emf {Ev} V and internal resistance {r} Ω is connected to a {R} Ω load. Find the current (A), the terminal voltage (V) and the power delivered to the load (W), to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$I = \dfrac{\mathcal{E}}{R + r} = \dfrac{{Ev}}{{R} + {r}} =$ **{I:num4} A**.

$V = \mathcal{E} - Ir =$ **{Vt:num2} V**; $P = I^2R =$ **{P:num2} W**.

drills.title: Two-battery circuit (Kirchhoff's rules)
drills.prompt: Three branches connect junctions A (top) and B (bottom). Branch 1: a {E1} V battery and a {R1} Ω resistor. Branch 2: a {E2} V battery and a {R2} Ω resistor. Branch 3: a {R3} Ω resistor alone. Both batteries have their $+$ terminal toward A. Taking $I_1$, $I_2$ as upward currents in branches 1 and 2 and $I_3$ as the downward current in branch 3, find all three in amperes to 3 significant figures (a negative value means the opposite direction).
drills.solution:
Junction A: $I_3 = I_1 + I_2$. Loop 1–3: ${E1} - {R1}I_1 - {R3}I_3 = 0$. Loop 2–3: ${E2} - {R2}I_2 - {R3}I_3 = 0$.

Substituting: $({R1} + {R3})I_1 + {R3}I_2 = {E1}$ and ${R3}I_1 + ({R2} + {R3})I_2 = {E2}$. Solve these two equations simultaneously, for example by multiplying the first by ${R3}$ and the second by $({R1} + {R3})$ and subtracting to eliminate $I_1$.

$I_1 =$ **{I1:num4} A**, $I_2 =$ **{I2:num4} A**, $I_3 = I_1 + I_2 =$ **{I3:num4} A**.

drills.title: Charging a capacitor
drills.prompt: A {C} μF capacitor, initially uncharged, charges through a {R} kΩ resistor from a {Ev} V battery. Find the time constant (s), and the capacitor's voltage (V) and the current (mA) at $t = {t:num4}$ s. Give 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\tau = RC = ({R}\times10^3)({C}\times10^{-6}) =$ **{tau:num4} s**, so $t/\tau = {t:num4}/{tau:num4} = {n}$.

$V_C = \mathcal{E}(1 - e^{-t/\tau}) = {Ev}(1 - e^{-{n}}) =$ **{V:num2} V**.

$I = \dfrac{\mathcal{E}}{\,R}e^{-t/\tau} =$ **{I:sig3} mA**.

drills.title: Discharge time of a capacitor
drills.prompt: A {C:dp0} μF capacitor charged to {V0} V discharges through a {R} kΩ resistor. How long until its voltage falls to {Vf:num1} V ({pct}% of the start)? Give seconds to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $\tau = RC = {tau:sig3}$ s. From $V = V_0e^{-t/\tau}$: $t = \tau\ln\dfrac{V_0}{V} = {tau:sig3}\ln\dfrac{100}{{pct}} =$ **{t:sig3} s**.

drills.title: Charged particle circling in a magnetic field
drills.prompt: Consider {part} moving at ${vm}\times10^{{ve}}$ m/s perpendicular to a {B} T magnetic field. Find the magnetic force on it and the radius of its circular path, each to 3 significant figures. ($e = 1.602\times10^{-19}$ C, $m_e = 9.11\times10^{-31}$ kg, $m_p = 1.673\times10^{-27}$ kg)
drills.solution:
$F = |q|vB = (1.602\times10^{-19})({vm}\times10^{{ve}})({B}) = \mathbf{{F:texsci}}$ N.

$r = \dfrac{mv}{|q|B} = \dfrac{({mcoef:sig4}\times10^{{mexp}})({vm}\times10^{{ve}})}{(1.602\times10^{-19})({B})} = \mathbf{{r:texsci}}$ m.

drills.title: Force on a current-carrying wire
drills.prompt: A straight wire {L} m long carries {I} A in a uniform {B} T magnetic field. The wire makes an angle of {th}° with the field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on it, in newtons to 3 significant figures?
drills.solution: $F = ILB\sin\theta = ({I})({L})({B})\sin {th}^\circ =$ **{F:sig3} N**, perpendicular to both the wire and the field.

drills.title: Mass spectrometer radius
drills.prompt: A singly charged ion of mass {A} u ($1\text{ u} = 1.661\times10^{-27}$ kg) is accelerated from rest through {V:dp0} V and enters a {B} T magnetic field perpendicular to its velocity. Find its speed (m/s) and the radius of its path (cm), each to 3 significant figures. ($e = 1.602\times10^{-19}$ C)
drills.solution:
$m = {A}(1.661\times10^{-27}) = {m:texsci}$ kg. From $\tfrac12mv^2 = eV$: $v = \sqrt{2eV/m} = \mathbf{{v:texsci}}$ m/s.

$r = \dfrac{mv}{eB} = {r:texsci}$ m $=$ **{rcm:num2} cm**.

drills.title: Magnetic field of a long straight wire
drills.prompt: A long straight wire carries {I:dp0} A. Find the magnetic field {rcm} cm from it, in microtesla to 3 significant figures. ($\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}$ T·m/A)
drills.solution: $B = \dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r} = \dfrac{(4\pi\times10^{-7})({I:dp0})}{2\pi({rcm}/100)} = {B:texsci}$ T $=$ **{BuT:sig3} μT**.

drills.title: Field inside a solenoid
drills.prompt: A long solenoid {lcm} cm long has {N:dp0} turns and carries {I} A. Find the number of turns per meter and the magnetic field inside (in mT), each to 3 significant figures. ($\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}$ T·m/A)
drills.solution:
Turns per meter: $n = \dfrac{\,N}{\ell} = \dfrac{{N:dp0}}{{lcm}/100\text{ m}} =$ **{n:sig4} turns/m**.

$B = \mu_0nI = (4\pi\times10^{-7})({n:sig4})({I}) =$ **{BmT:sig3} mT**. Use turns per meter, not the total number of turns.

drills.title: Force between parallel wires
drills.prompt: Two long parallel wires {dcm} cm apart carry {I1} A and {I2} A in the same direction. Find the force per meter between them in mN/m, to 3 significant figures. (Then decide: is it attractive or repulsive?)
drills.solution: $\dfrac FL = \dfrac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d} = \dfrac{(2\times10^{-7})({I1})({I2})}{{dcm}/100} =$ **{FmN:sig3} mN/m**, attractive (currents in the same direction attract).

drills.title: Induced emf in a coil
drills.prompt: A {N:dp0}-turn coil of area {A:dp3} m² lies perpendicular to a magnetic field that changes steadily from {B1} T to {B2} T in {t} s. Find the magnitude of the induced emf (V) and, if the coil's resistance is {R} Ω, the induced current (A), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$|\Delta\Phi_B| = |{B2} - {B1}|({A:dp3})$ Wb per turn.

$|\mathcal{E}| = N\dfrac{|\Delta\Phi_B|}{\Delta t} =$ **{emf:sig3} V**; $I = \mathcal{E}/R =$ **{I:sig3} A**, directed to oppose the change in flux.

drills.title: Sliding rod on rails
drills.prompt: A rod {L} m long slides at {v} m/s along conducting rails in a {B} T field perpendicular to the rails. The rails are joined by a {R} Ω resistor. Find the emf (V), the current (A), and the force (N) needed to keep the rod moving at constant speed, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\mathcal{E} = BLv = ({B})({L})({v}) =$ **{emf:num4} V**; $I = \mathcal{E}/R =$ **{I:num4} A**.

The field pushes back on the current with $F = ILB$, so you must push with **{F:num4} N** (power $Fv = I^2R$).

drills.title: Ideal transformer
drills.prompt: An ideal transformer has {Np:dp0} primary turns and {Ns:dp0} secondary turns, with {Vp:dp0} V (rms) on the primary. Find the secondary voltage (V) and, if the secondary delivers {Is} A, the primary current (A), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$V_s = V_p\dfrac{N_s}{N_p} = {Vp:dp0}\cdot\dfrac{{Ns:dp0}}{{Np:dp0}} =$ **{Vs:sig3} V**.

Power is conserved: $I_p = \dfrac{V_sI_s}{V_p} =$ **{Ip:sig3} A**.

drills.title: RL circuit current growth
drills.prompt: A {L} H inductor and a {R} Ω resistor are connected in series to a {Ev} V battery at $t = 0$. Find the time constant (ms), the final current (A), and the current (A) at $t = {tms:sig3}$ ms, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\tau = L/R = {L}/{R}$ s $=$ **{taums:sig3} ms**. Final current $\mathcal{E}/R = {Ev}/{R} =$ **{Imax:sig3} A**.

$t/\tau = {tms:sig3}/{taums:sig4} = {ratio:num4}$, so $I = \dfrac{\mathcal{E}}{\,R}(1 - e^{-t/\tau}) = {Imax:sig4}(1 - e^{-{ratio:num4}}) =$ **{I:sig3} A**.

drills.title: LC resonant frequency
drills.prompt: An LC circuit has a {L} mH inductor and a {C:dp0} nF capacitor. Find its resonant frequency in kHz, to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{({L}\times10^{-3})({C:dp0}\times10^{-9})}} =$ **{fk:sig3} kHz**.

drills.title: RMS values and reactance
drills.prompt: An AC source has peak voltage {V0} V and frequency {f} Hz. Find (a) its rms voltage, (b) the average power it delivers to a {R} Ω resistor, and (c) the reactance of a {C} μF capacitor at this frequency. Give each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) $V_{\text{rms}} = V_0/\sqrt2 =$ **{Vr:num2} V**.

(b) $P = V_{\text{rms}}^2/R =$ **{P:sig3} W** (not $V_0^2/R$, which is the peak power).

(c) $X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi fC} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi({f:dp0})({C}\times10^{-6})} =$ **{XC:sig3} Ω**.

drills.title: Wavelength and frequency of EM waves
drills.prompt: An electromagnetic wave in vacuum has frequency ${fm}\times10^{{fe}}$ Hz. What is its wavelength in meters, to 3 significant figures? ($c = 3.00\times10^8$ m/s)
drills.solution: $\lambda = \dfrac{c}{\,f} = \dfrac{3.00\times10^8}{{fm}\times10^{{fe}}} = \mathbf{{lam:texsci}}$ m. (Radio and microwaves have long wavelengths; visible light is a few hundred nanometers; X-rays are far shorter.)

drills.title: Snell's law
drills.prompt: Light in {m1} (n = {m1:num2}) strikes {m2} at {t1}° from the normal. Find the angle of refraction (to the nearest 0.1°) and the speed of light in the second material (m/s, 3 significant figures). ($c = 3.00\times10^8$ m/s)
drills.solution:
$n_1\sin\theta_1 = n_2\sin\theta_2$: $\sin\theta_2 = \dfrac{{m1:num2}\sin {t1}^\circ}{{m2:num2}}$, so $\theta_2 =$ **{t2:num1}°** (bent toward the normal).

$v = c/n = \mathbf{{v:texsci}}$ m/s.

drills.title: Critical angle for total internal reflection
drills.prompt: Light travels inside a material with $n = {n1}$ toward a boundary with {out}. What is the critical angle for total internal reflection, to the nearest 0.1°?
drills.solution: $\sin\theta_c = \dfrac{n_2}{n_1} = \dfrac{{out:num2}}{{n1}}$, so $\theta_c =$ **{tc:num1}°**. Rays hitting the boundary at more than this angle (from the normal) are totally reflected.

drills.title: Light through polarizers
drills.prompt: Unpolarized light of intensity {I0:dp0} W/m² passes through a polarizer, then a second polarizer whose axis is at {th}° to the first. Find the intensity after each polarizer, in W/m² to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The first polarizer passes half of unpolarized light: $I_1 = {I0:dp0}/2 =$ **{I1:num1} W/m²**.

Malus's law: $I_2 = I_1\cos^2\theta = {I1:num1}\cos^2 {th}^\circ =$ **{I2:num2} W/m²**.

drills.title: Thin lens image
drills.prompt: A {ho} cm tall object stands {dob} cm from a thin lens of focal length {f} cm (negative = diverging). Find the image distance in cm (negative = virtual, same side as the object) and the magnification, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\dfrac1{d_i} = \dfrac1f - \dfrac1{d_o} = \dfrac{1}{{f}} - \dfrac{1}{{dob}}$, so $d_i =$ **{di:num2} cm**.

$m = -\dfrac{d_i}{d_o} =$ **{m:num4}**, so the image is {hi:num2} cm tall (negative means inverted). A positive $d_i$ is a real image on the far side.

drills.title: Spherical mirror image
drills.prompt: An object is {dob} cm in front of a {kind} mirror with radius of curvature {R} cm. Find the image distance in cm (negative = behind the mirror, virtual) and the magnification, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$f = \pm R/2$, positive for concave and negative for convex: $f = {f}$ cm.

$\dfrac1{d_i} = \dfrac1f - \dfrac1{d_o}$, so $d_i =$ **{di:num2} cm**; $m = -d_i/d_o =$ **{m:num4}**.

drills.title: Two-lens system
drills.prompt: An object is {d1} cm in front of a converging lens ($f_1 = {f1}$ cm). A second converging lens ($f_2 = {f2}$ cm) is {sep} cm beyond the first. Find the final image distance from the second lens (cm) and the overall magnification, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
Lens 1: $d_{i1} = \left(\dfrac{1}{{f1}} - \dfrac{1}{{d1}}\right)^{-1} = {img1:num2}$ cm, with $m_1 = -d_{i1}/d_{o1} = {mag1:num4}$.

That image is the object for lens 2, at $d_{o2} = {sep} - {img1:num2} = {obj2:num2}$ cm.

Lens 2: $d_{i2} = \left(\dfrac{1}{{f2}} - \dfrac{1}{{obj2:num2}}\right)^{-1} =$ **{img2:num2} cm**.

Total $m = m_1m_2 = \left(-\dfrac{d_{i1}}{d_{o1}}\right)\left(-\dfrac{d_{i2}}{d_{o2}}\right) =$ **{m:num4}**.

drills.title: Simple magnifier
drills.prompt: A magnifying glass has a focal length of {fl:num1} cm, and the viewer's near point is 25 cm. Find its angular magnification (a) with the image at infinity and (b) with the image at the near point, and (c) the object's distance from the lens in case (b), in cm. Give each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) Object at the focal point, image at infinity: $M = \dfrac{25\text{ cm}}{f} = \dfrac{25}{{fl:num1}} =$ **{M1:sig3}**.

(b) Image at the near point: $M = 1 + \dfrac{25\text{ cm}}{f} =$ **{M2:sig3}**.

(c) With $d_i = -25$ cm, $\dfrac1{d_o} = \dfrac1f - \dfrac1{d_i} = \dfrac{1}{{fl:num1}} + \dfrac{1}{25}$, so $d_o = \dfrac{25({fl:num1})}{25 + {fl:num1}} =$ **{dob:sig3} cm**, just inside the focal length.

drills.title: Compound microscope
drills.prompt: A compound microscope has an objective of focal length {fo:num2} cm and an eyepiece of focal length {fe:num1} cm, mounted {sep} cm apart. It is adjusted so the final image is at infinity (near point 25 cm). Find (a) the specimen's distance from the objective (cm), (b) the objective's magnification and (c) the overall angular magnification (negative = inverted), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
For a final image at infinity, the objective's image sits at the eyepiece's focal point: $d_i = {sep} - {fe:num1} = {dio:num1}$ cm from the objective.

(a) $\dfrac1{d_o} = \dfrac1{f_o} - \dfrac1{d_i} = \dfrac{1}{{fo:num2}} - \dfrac{1}{{dio:num1}}$, so $d_o =$ **{doo:dp3} cm**, just outside $f_o$.

(b) $m_{\text{obj}} = -\dfrac{d_i}{d_o} = -\dfrac{{dio:num1}}{{doo:num4}} =$ **{mo:sig3}**.

(c) The eyepiece gives $M_e = 25/{fe:num1} = {Me:num2}$, so $M = m_{\text{obj}}M_e =$ **{Mt:sig3}**.

drills.title: Refracting telescope
drills.prompt: A refracting telescope has an objective of focal length {fo} cm and an eyepiece of focal length {fe:num1} cm, adjusted for viewing with a relaxed eye. Find its angular magnification (negative = inverted) and the distance between the lenses (cm), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$M = -\dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = -\dfrac{{fo}}{{fe:num1}} =$ **{M:sig3}**.

The objective's image lies at both lenses' focal points, so the lenses are $f_o + f_e = {fo} + {fe:num1} =$ **{len:sig3} cm** apart.

drills.title: Double-slit fringes
drills.prompt: Light of wavelength {lam:dp0} nm falls on two slits {dmm} mm apart; the screen is {L} m away. Find the fringe spacing in mm and the angle of the order-{mo} bright fringe in degrees, each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\Delta y = \dfrac{\lambda L}{d} = \dfrac{({lam:dp0}\times10^{-9})({L})}{{dmm}\times10^{-3}} =$ **{dy:num2} mm**.

$\sin\theta = \dfrac{m\lambda}{d} = \dfrac{{mo}({lam:dp0}\times10^{-9})}{{dmm}\times10^{-3}}$, so $\theta =$ **{ang:num4}°**.

drills.title: Diffraction grating
drills.prompt: A grating has {N:dp0} lines per mm and is lit with {lam:dp0} nm light. Find the angle of the first-order maximum (to the nearest 0.1°) and the highest order that appears on a screen in front of the grating.
drills.solution:
$d = \dfrac{1}{{N:dp0}\text{ mm}^{-1}} = {d:texsci}$ m. $\sin\theta_1 = \lambda/d$, so $\theta_1 =$ **{t1:num1}°**.

A maximum needs $\sin\theta = m\lambda/d < 1$ (an order with $\sin\theta = 1$ would travel along the grating's surface, never reaching the screen), so $m < d/\lambda = {ratio:num4}$. The highest order is **{mmax}**.

drills.title: Thin film color
drills.prompt: A thin film with $n = {n}$ surrounded by air strongly reflects {lam:dp0} nm light. Find the film thickness in nm, to 3 significant figures, for constructive order $m = {mm}$ (where $m = 0$ is the thinnest such film).
drills.solution:
Only the top reflection flips phase, so bright reflection needs $2nt = (m + \tfrac12)\lambda$.

$t = \dfrac{({mm} + 0.5)({lam:dp0})}{2({n})} =$ **{t:num1} nm**.

drills.title: Time dilation
drills.prompt: A spacecraft moves at ${b:dp3}c$ relative to Earth. A clock on board measures {t0} μs between two ticks. Find the Lorentz factor (4 significant figures) and the time between those ticks measured from Earth (μs, 3 significant figures).
drills.solution:
$\gamma = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - ({b:dp3})^2}} =$ **{gam:num4}**.

The ship's clock measures proper time, so $\Delta t = \gamma\Delta t_0 = {gam:num4}({t0}) =$ **{t:num2} μs**.

drills.title: Length contraction
drills.prompt: A spaceship has a proper length of {L0} m. What length do observers measure as it passes at ${b}c$? Give meters to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution: $L = L_0\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2} = {L0}\sqrt{1 - ({b})^2} =$ **{L:num2} m** (only the length along the motion contracts).

drills.title: Relativistic energy and momentum
drills.prompt: Consider {part} moving at ${b}c$. Find its total energy (MeV), kinetic energy (MeV) and momentum (in MeV/$c$), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\gamma = 1/\sqrt{1 - ({b})^2} = {gam:num4}$.

$E = \gamma mc^2 =$ **{E:num4} MeV**; $K = (\gamma - 1)mc^2 =$ **{K:num4} MeV**; $pc = \gamma mc^2(v/c) =$ **{pc:num4} MeV**, so $p$ = {pc:num4} MeV/$c$.

drills.title: Photon energy and photon rate
drills.prompt: A {PmW} mW light source emits {lam:dp0} nm light. Find the energy of each photon in eV and the number of photons emitted per second, each to 3 significant figures. ($hc = 1240$ eV·nm, $1\text{ eV} = 1.602\times10^{-19}$ J)
drills.solution:
$E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \dfrac{1240}{{lam:dp0}} =$ **{EeV:num4} eV** $= {EJ:texsci}$ J.

Rate $= \dfrac{P}{E} = \dfrac{{PmW}\times10^{-3}}{{EJ:texsci}} = \mathbf{{N:texsci}}$ photons/s.

drills.title: Photoelectric effect
drills.prompt: Light of wavelength {lam:dp0} nm shines on {metal}. Find the maximum kinetic energy of the ejected electrons (eV) and the metal's threshold wavelength (nm), each to 3 significant figures. ($hc = 1240$ eV·nm)
drills.solution:
Photon energy: $1240/{lam:dp0} = {E:num4}$ eV. $K_{\max} = hf - \phi = {E:num4} - {metal:num2} =$ **{K:num4} eV** (stopping potential {K:num4} V).

Threshold: $\lambda_0 = hc/\phi = 1240/{metal:num2} =$ **{l0:num1} nm**.

drills.title: Blackbody peak (Wien's law)
drills.prompt: Treat each object as a blackbody, with $\lambda_{\max}T = 2.898\times10^{-3}$ m·K. (a) A star's surface is at {temp:dp0} K. At what wavelength (nm) does its spectrum peak? (b) Another object's spectrum peaks at {lam2:dp0} nm. What is its temperature (K)? Give each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) $\lambda_{\max} = \dfrac{2.898\times10^{-3}\text{ m·K}}{{temp:dp0}\text{ K}} = {lmaxm:texsci}$ m $=$ **{lmax:sig3} nm**.

(b) $T = \dfrac{2.898\times10^{-3}}{{lam2:dp0}\times10^{-9}} =$ **{T2:sig3} K**.

drills.title: Compton scattering
drills.prompt: An X-ray photon of wavelength {lam:num1} pm scatters off a nearly free electron and leaves at {th}° to its original direction. Using $h/(m_ec) = 2.43$ pm and $hc = 1240$ keV·pm, find (a) the wavelength shift (pm), (b) the scattered wavelength (pm) and (c) the kinetic energy given to the electron (keV), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
(a) $\Delta\lambda = \dfrac{h}{m_ec}(1 - \cos\theta) = 2.43(1 - \cos{th}^\circ) =$ **{dl:sig3} pm**.

(b) $\lambda' = \lambda + \Delta\lambda = {lam:num1} + {dl:num4} =$ **{lp:sig3} pm**.

(c) The electron gains the energy the photon loses: $K = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda'} = \dfrac{1240}{{lam:num1}} - \dfrac{1240}{{lp:num4}} =$ **{Ke:sig3} keV**. (Keep extra digits: the two energies are close.)

drills.title: Hydrogen transition (Bohr model)
drills.prompt: A hydrogen atom's electron drops from $n = {ni}$ to $n = {nf}$. Find the energy (eV) and wavelength (nm) of the emitted photon, each to 4 significant figures. ($E_n = -13.6\text{ eV}/n^2$, $hc = 1240$ eV·nm)
drills.solution:
$\Delta E = 13.6\left(\dfrac{1}{{nf}^2} - \dfrac{1}{{ni}^2}\right) =$ **{dE:num4} eV**.

$\lambda = 1240/\Delta E =$ **{lam:num1} nm** (visible if between about 400 and 700 nm; transitions to $n = 1$ are ultraviolet).

drills.title: de Broglie wavelength of an accelerated particle
drills.prompt: Starting from rest, {part} is accelerated through {V:dp0} V. Find its de Broglie wavelength in nm, to 3 significant figures (ignore relativistic effects). ($h = 6.63\times10^{-34}$ J·s, $e = 1.602\times10^{-19}$ C, $m_e = 9.11\times10^{-31}$ kg, $m_p = 1.673\times10^{-27}$ kg)
drills.solution:
$K = eV$ and $p = \sqrt{2mK} = \sqrt{2({part:texsci})(1.602\times10^{-19})({V:dp0})} = {p:texsci}$ kg·m/s.

$\lambda = \dfrac hp = {lam:texsci}$ m $= \mathbf{{lnm:texsci}}$ nm.

drills.title: Counting quantum states
drills.prompt: Consider the {n}{sub} subshell of an atom. Give (a) its orbital quantum number $l$, (b) the number of allowed $m_l$ values, (c) the greatest number of electrons the subshell can hold, and (d) the greatest number of electrons the whole $n = {n}$ shell can hold.
drills.solution:
(a) The letters s, p, d, f stand for $l = 0, 1, 2, 3$, so {sub} means $l =$ **{lval:int}**.

(b) $m_l$ runs from $-l$ to $l$, so the number of values is $2l + 1 =$ **{nml:int}**.

(c) Each $m_l$ allows two spins ($m_s = \pm\tfrac12$), so the subshell holds $2(2l + 1) =$ **{esub:int}** electrons (Pauli exclusion principle).

(d) The shell holds $2n^2 = 2({n})^2 =$ **{eshell:int}** electrons.

drills.title: X-ray tube cutoff
drills.prompt: An X-ray tube accelerates electrons through {kV} kV. Find (a) the energy of the most energetic X-ray photon (keV), (b) the cutoff wavelength (pm) and (c) the highest X-ray frequency (Hz), each to 3 significant figures. ($hc = 1240$ eV·nm, $h = 6.63\times10^{-34}$ J·s, $e = 1.602\times10^{-19}$ C)
drills.solution:
(a) The most energetic photon takes all of an electron's kinetic energy, $eV$: **{Emax} keV**.

(b) $\lambda_{\min} = \dfrac{hc}{eV}$. With $hc = 1240$ eV·nm $= 1240$ keV·pm, $\lambda_{\min} = \dfrac{1240\text{ keV·pm}}{{kV}\text{ keV}} =$ **{lmin:sig3} pm**.

(c) $f_{\max} = \dfrac{eV}{h} = \dfrac{(1.602\times10^{-19})({kV}\times10^{3})}{6.63\times10^{-34}} = \mathbf{{fmax:texsci}}$ Hz.

drills.title: Characteristic X-ray (Kα) estimate
drills.prompt: Estimate the energy (keV) and wavelength (pm) of the Kα X-ray line of {el}, using $E \approx 10.2\text{ eV}\,(Z - 1)^2$ and $hc = 1240$ eV·nm. Give each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
The remaining 1s electron screens one unit of nuclear charge, so the dropping electron sees about $Z - 1 = {el:dp0} - 1$.

$E \approx 10.2({el:dp0} - 1)^2 = {EeV:dp0}$ eV $=$ **{EkeV:sig3} keV**.

$\lambda = \dfrac{hc}{E} = \dfrac{1240\text{ eV·nm}}{{EeV:dp0}\text{ eV}} = {lamnm:num4}$ nm $=$ **{lam:sig3} pm**.

drills.title: Radioactive decay
drills.prompt: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of {T} days. A sample starts with activity {A0:dp0} MBq. Find the decay constant (per day) and the activity after {t} days (MBq), each to 3 significant figures.
drills.solution:
$\lambda = \dfrac{\ln 2}{T_{1/2}} = \dfrac{0.693}{{T}} =$ **{lam:num4} per day**.

$A = A_0\left(\tfrac12\right)^{t/T_{1/2}} = {A0:dp0}\left(\tfrac12\right)^{{t}/{T}} =$ **{A:num2} MBq**.

drills.title: Nuclear binding energy
drills.prompt: Find the mass defect (u), binding energy (MeV) and binding energy per nucleon (MeV) of {nuc}, each to 4 significant figures. Use hydrogen-atom mass 1.007825 u, neutron mass 1.008665 u, and 1 u = 931.5 MeV/$c^2$.
drills.solution:
Separate parts: ${Z}(1.007825) + {N}(1.008665) = {mtot:dp6}$ u.

Mass defect: $\Delta m = {mtot:dp6} - {nuc:dp6} =$ **{dm:dp6} u**.

$E_B = \Delta m\,(931.5\text{ MeV/u}) =$ **{EB:num2} MeV**, or **{per:num4} MeV** per nucleon.

drills.title: Carbon dating
drills.prompt: A sample of ancient charcoal has {pct}% of the carbon-14 activity of living wood. Using a half-life of 5730 years, how old is it, in years to 3 significant figures?
drills.solution: $\dfrac{A}{A_0} = \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t/5730}$, so $t = 5730\cdot\dfrac{\ln({pct}/100)}{\ln 0.5} =$ **{t:dp0} years**.
